source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-3

procedures.title: Corvette rear suspension: general description
notes: Independent three-link layout: the differential carrier is fixed and rubber mounted to the frame at 3 points; at each wheel the strut rod, drive shaft and torque control arm form the three links, with a multi-leaf spring mounted crosswise (see figure 5 in the manual).
The torque control arms are box-section trailing arms; their front ends sit in openings in the frame side members on pivot bolts and rubber bushings, and their rear ends connect to the leaf spring.
Each wheel spindle and spindle support bolts to its torque control arm with 4 bolts pressed into the arm.
Rear toe-in is set with shims of different thicknesses fitted between the torque arm and the frame side member web at the front pivot.
